option_description: Whether indexed events and audit records are tamper-evident via integrity hashing or WORM/append-only storage (e.g. Splunk indexes.conf enableDataIntegrityControl=true, SHA-256 per 128KB slice).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Log tampering / deletion to blind detection" — fires when audit_log_tamper_evident is false, leaving a compromised host or admin able to silently delete or alter the security record (T1070 Indicator Removal).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep the Splunk indexes.conf for the per-index data-integrity control. Note the dossier caveat: the default is false and it only protects data indexed AFTER enabling.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: enableDataIntegrityControl = true per index (secure: SHA-256 hashes computed per 128KB slice for tamper-evidence) vs absent/false (insecure default — no integrity hashing)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the stored hashes actually match the buckets for the index.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Integrity verification PASS for the index's buckets (secure) vs hash mismatch / 'no hash files' (tampering or integrity control never enabled)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm whether, instead of (or in addition to) hashing, the index data is written to an immutable/WORM or append-only remote store.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Audit evidence that detection logs are forwarded to a remote/immutable repository per ATT&CK M1029 Remote Data Storage so a compromised source host cannot locate and manipulate them
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1070 Indicator Removal (M1029 Remote Data Storage)

option_description: Whether the end-to-end log/event pipeline (ingest through index) is integrity-protected so events cannot be modified, dropped, or forged between source and durable store (hash-chaining / signed forwarding / verified ingest).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Log tampering / deletion to blind detection" — fires when log_pipeline_integrity_protected is false, letting events be altered in transit or at index time without detection.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Splunk forwarding/index TLS stanza — signed/verified forwarding over enableSplunkdSSL is the pipeline-integrity enforcement point.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: enableSplunkdSSL = true with operator-supplied serverCert (secure) vs disabled or the bundled demo cert still in place (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: Splunk About securing the Splunk platform (server.conf [sslConfig] enableSplunkdSSL; replace default certificates)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify per-index integrity hashing covers the durable store end of the pipeline.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Integrity verification PASS for the index's buckets (secure) vs hash mismatch / 'no hash files' (no end-to-end integrity)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the pipeline design for hash-chaining or signed forwarding from source to durable index.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented hash-chaining / signed-forwarding / verified-ingest design proving events cannot be modified or forged between source and store
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1070 Indicator Removal (M1029 Remote Data Storage)

option_description: Whether security events are forwarded to and retained on a remote/immutable repository separate from the monitored hosts (ATT&CK M1029 Remote Data Storage).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Log tampering / deletion to blind detection" — fires when logs_stored_on_separate_system is false, leaving indexed events on locally mutable disk reachable by anyone who compromises the source or SIEM host.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm security events are forwarded off-host to a remote/immutable repository per ATT&CK M1029.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Audit evidence that detection logs are forwarded to a remote/immutable repository per ATT&CK M1029 Remote Data Storage so a compromised source host cannot locate and manipulate them
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1070 Indicator Removal (M1029 Remote Data Storage)

how_to_obtain.instruction: On a monitored host, verify the local forwarder ships to a remote indexer rather than writing only locally.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Active forward-server(s) pointing to a remote indexer tier (secure) vs no forwarding / local-only indexing (insecure)

option_description: Whether file-integrity monitoring watches the index/audit data files and configuration so unauthorized deletion or modification of the security record is itself detected and alerted.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Log tampering / deletion to blind detection" — fires when file_integrity_monitoring_enabled is false, so tampering with the stored events leaves no secondary trace.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check Wazuh syscheck (FIM) coverage of the SIEM index/audit data and config directories in ossec.conf.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: syscheck enabled with <directories> entries covering the index/audit data and SIEM config paths (secure) vs syscheck disabled or no coverage of the log store (insecure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm FIM (or equivalent integrity alerting) raises an alert on modification/deletion of the index/audit files, not merely records it.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Evidence of an active FIM alert covering the log store, with a sample fired/test alert on change to a watched file

option_description: Whether correlation/detection rules (saved/correlation searches) exist, are enabled, scheduled, and tuned to relevant ATT&CK coverage — not an empty or all-disabled rule set.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Detection / alerting disabled or silently failing" — fires when detection_rules_present_and_enabled is false (collection without detection — the most common silent blinding).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Count enabled, scheduled saved/correlation searches via the REST endpoint.
how_to_obtain.command: splunk search '| rest /servicesNS/-/-/saved/searches | search is_scheduled=1 disabled=0 | stats count'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A non-trivial count of enabled scheduled/correlation searches (secure) vs zero or all disabled (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: Splunk About securing the Splunk platform (saved/correlation searches)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the enabled rules map to relevant ATT&CK technique coverage and are tuned (not just present).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented detection-coverage mapping showing enabled rules align to the threats the deployment must detect

option_description: Whether all security-relevant sources forward their events to the SIEM with documented coverage and a missing-source/liveness alert (CIS Control 8.2), so a stopped or absent feed is not a silent blind spot.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for both "Detection / alerting disabled or silently failing" and "Unmasked secrets/PII in the index; coverage and retention gaps" — fires when security_events_fully_logged is false (forwarders/host logging stopped, T1562.001/.002).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Compare expected sources against sources actually reporting recent events.
how_to_obtain.command: splunk search 'index=* | tstats count where index=* by host | inputlookup expected_sources | ... compare'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Every expected source has recent events; a 'source has not reported in N hours' alert exists (secure) vs no liveness monitoring (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 Audit Log Management (8.2 collect audit logs)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the documented log-source inventory and confirm gaps are mapped against the asset inventory.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented log-management process and source inventory reviewed per CIS 8.1; gaps mapped against the asset inventory
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 Audit Log Management (8.1)

option_description: Whether the SIEM raises an alert when its own detection/logging pipeline fails — skipped scheduled searches, failed alert actions, or ingestion stalls are surfaced rather than going unnoticed.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Detection / alerting disabled or silently failing" — fires when logging_failure_alerting_enabled is false, so scheduler errors / skipped correlation searches accumulate silently and detections quietly stop firing.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the internal scheduler log for skipped or errored scheduled searches.
how_to_obtain.command: splunk search 'index=_internal sourcetype=scheduler (status=skipped OR status=delegated_remote_error) | stats count by savedsearch_name'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Low/zero skipped scheduled searches and a working heartbeat alert (secure) vs many skipped/errored searches (insecure — alerts silently not firing)
how_to_obtain.source: Splunk About securing the Splunk platform (scheduler/_internal monitoring)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm an alert exists that fires ON pipeline failure (skipped-search ratio / ingest stall), not merely a dashboard a human must check.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An active alert on scheduler skip ratio / failed alert actions / ingestion stalls, with evidence of delivery

option_description: Whether the alert delivery path (email/webhook/ticketing/SOAR) is monitored end-to-end with a heartbeat/self-test that proves delivery.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Detection / alerting disabled or silently failing" — fires when alert_delivery_path_monitored is false, so a broken notification channel blinds the SOC the same way deleting logs would.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check for skipped/errored alert actions on the delivery path in the scheduler/internal logs.
how_to_obtain.command: splunk search 'index=_internal sourcetype=scheduler (status=skipped OR status=delegated_remote_error) | stats count by savedsearch_name'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Low/zero failed alert actions plus a working heartbeat alert (secure) vs failed actions and no delivery confirmation (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: Splunk About securing the Splunk platform (scheduler/_internal monitoring)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a periodic heartbeat/self-test alert must actually ARRIVE at the destination channel (mailbox/ticket/SOAR), proving end-to-end delivery.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Evidence of a scheduled heartbeat alert whose absence at the destination triggers escalation

option_description: Whether only authenticated, enrolled forwarders/agents may submit events to the ingest channel (e.g. Wazuh authd use_password=yes AND ssl_agent_ca with ssl_verify_host=yes — mutual enrollment authentication).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Spoofed / injected or unencrypted log ingestion" — fires when authenticated_log_forwarders_required is false (open enrollment), letting any host inject forged events to poison detection or bury real alerts.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Wazuh manager <auth> enrollment block in ossec.conf for password + certificate enrollment.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: <use_password>yes</use_password>, <ssl_agent_ca> set, <ssl_verify_host>yes</ssl_verify_host> (secure) vs use_password=no and no CA / ssl_verify_host=no (insecure default — open enrollment)

how_to_obtain.instruction: For a Splunk deployment, confirm forwarders authenticate (token/cert-based forwarding) rather than accepting anonymous inputs.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Evidence that ingest accepts only enrolled/authenticated forwarders; no open/anonymous receiving port

option_description: Whether incoming log events are validated/sanitized at ingest so a malicious or unauthenticated source cannot inject forged or crafted events that corrupt parsing, spoof source identity, or bury real alerts.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Spoofed / injected or unencrypted log ingestion" — fires when log_injection_input_sanitized is false (raw payloads indexed verbatim with no source/content validation), enabling event forgery and noise floods.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the ingest/parsing config for source-identity binding and content validation (props.conf/transforms.conf or equivalent ingest filters).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Ingest-time transforms validating/normalizing source and content (secure) vs no validation, raw payloads indexed verbatim (insecure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm ingest binds events to an authenticated source identity so a sender cannot spoof another host's identity field.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Evidence that source identity is enforced at ingest and crafted/forged payloads are rejected or quarantined

option_description: Whether TLS 1.2+ is enforced on all log-ingest and enrollment channels with operator-supplied (non-default) certificates so events cannot be carried in cleartext; plaintext syslog/UDP 514 refused.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for BOTH "Spoofed / injected or unencrypted log ingestion" and "Cleartext / weak-TLS ingest transport" — fires when tls_only_transport is false (plaintext or unencrypted ingest accepted), exposing events to disclosure, modification, and masquerade (RFC 5425).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Splunk server.conf [sslConfig] stanza for splunkd SSL and a non-default certificate.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: enableSplunkdSSL = true with operator-supplied serverCert (secure) vs disabled or the bundled demo cert still in place (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: Splunk About securing the Splunk platform (server.conf [sslConfig] enableSplunkdSSL; replace default certificates)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe the indexer ingest port and confirm a TLS handshake completes (and that cleartext is refused).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: TLS handshake completes with the operator's certificate (secure) vs connection in cleartext or presenting the SplunkServerDefaultCert demo cert (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 5425 TLS Transport Mapping for Syslog

option_description: Whether the ingest/enrollment channel permits legacy downgradeable TLS (SSLv3/TLS1.0/1.1) or weak ciphers (ADH/EXP/MD5/RC4/3DES), e.g. Wazuh ssl_auto_negotiate=yes. Secure value is false (TLS 1.2+ HIGH ciphers only).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for BOTH "Spoofed / injected or unencrypted log ingestion" and "Cleartext / weak-TLS ingest transport" — fires when weak_tls_versions_enabled is true (auto-negotiate or legacy protocols/ciphers accepted), allowing an on-path attacker to force a weak negotiation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Wazuh <auth> block for protocol/cipher negotiation.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ssl_auto_negotiate=no (only TLS 1.2 allowed) with a HIGH cipher list excluding ADH/EXP/MD5/RC4/3DES (secure) vs ssl_auto_negotiate=yes (insecure — permits downgrade)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate the protocols/ciphers actually offered on the ingest/enrollment ports.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only TLSv1.2/1.3 with A-grade ciphers offered (secure) vs TLSv1.0/1.1 or weak ciphers present (insecure)

option_description: The lowest TLS protocol version the ingest/enrollment channel will negotiate. Secure: TLSv1.2 or TLSv1.3 (RFC 5425 mandates TLS 1.2+); insecure: SSLv3/TLSv1.0/TLSv1.1.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for the exposure "Cleartext / weak-TLS ingest transport" — the condition selects on the individual legacy values SSLv3/TLSv1.0/TLSv1.1, exposing the channel to downgrade and known protocol weaknesses.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the negotiated minimum on the Wazuh enrollment channel — ssl_auto_negotiate=no pins TLS 1.2 as the floor.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ssl_auto_negotiate=no (TLS 1.2 floor) (secure) vs ssl_auto_negotiate=yes permitting SSLv3/TLS1.0/1.1 (insecure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm on the wire that the lowest negotiable version is TLSv1.2 or TLSv1.3.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Lowest offered protocol is TLSv1.2 (or TLSv1.3) (secure) vs SSLv3/TLSv1.0/TLSv1.1 offered (insecure)

option_description: Whether the ingest endpoint presents and the peer validates an operator-supplied certificate rather than accepting bundled demo/default certificates (Splunk replaced SplunkServerDefaultCert; Wazuh ssl_verify_host=yes with ssl_agent_ca).
security_impact: An OR-trigger for the exposure "Cleartext / weak-TLS ingest transport" — fires when server_certificate_validated is false (default/demo cert or no validation), enabling on-path masquerade despite a TLS wrapper.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Connect to the ingest port and inspect the presented certificate — confirm it is not the bundled demo cert.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: TLS handshake completes with the operator's certificate (secure) vs presenting the SplunkServerDefaultCert demo cert (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 5425 TLS Transport Mapping for Syslog

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Wazuh, confirm certificate verification of the peer is mandatory.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: <ssl_agent_ca> set and <ssl_verify_host>yes</ssl_verify_host> (secure: peer cert validated against CA + CN/IP check) vs no CA / ssl_verify_host=no (insecure)

option_description: Whether interactive admin/analyst access to the SIEM console and API requires MFA (ideally via SAML/OIDC SSO to a phishing-resistant IdP).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Stolen credentials / weak RBAC on the SIEM" — fires when mfa_available is false (local password-only login), so stolen credentials alone reach the detection backbone (T1078 Valid Accounts).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm SIEM console/API logins are federated to an IdP that enforces MFA, with no local password-only privileged accounts.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Evidence that SIEM console/API logins are federated to an IdP enforcing MFA; no local password-only privileged accounts
how_to_obtain.source: Splunk About securing the Splunk platform (manage credentials and access)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check Splunk authentication.conf to confirm SAML/LDAP+MFA is the configured authentication backend rather than local Splunk auth.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: authType = SAML (or external IdP enforcing MFA) (secure) vs authType = Splunk local-only (insecure — password-only)

option_description: Whether custom least-privilege roles separate analyst (read/search) from admin (config/role management); analyst roles cannot alter config, delete data, or hold admin-equivalent capabilities (edit_*/admin_all_objects).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Stolen credentials / weak RBAC on the SIEM" — fires when least_privilege_access_enforced is false (over-broad roles), letting a compromised analyst or insider disable feeds, delete rules, or read masked data.

how_to_obtain.instruction: List users/roles and inspect authorize.conf capabilities to confirm analyst roles lack admin-equivalent capabilities.
how_to_obtain.command: splunk list user; splunk btool authorize list --debug
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Named per-person accounts mapped to scoped roles; analyst role lacks edit_* / admin_all_objects capabilities (secure) vs over-broad roles (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: Splunk About securing the Splunk platform (RBAC / secure the default admin account)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read authorize.conf directly to enumerate the capabilities granted to each custom role.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Custom analyst role with read/search capabilities only; admin capabilities confined to a separate role (secure) vs analyst granted edit_*/admin_all_objects (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: Splunk About securing the Splunk platform (RBAC / secure the default admin account)

option_description: Whether privileged SIEM access uses a shared admin account rather than named per-person accounts. Secure value is false (named accounts only).
security_impact: An OR-trigger for the exposure "Stolen credentials / weak RBAC on the SIEM" — fires when shared_admin_accounts is true, losing individual accountability so a leaked shared credential grants full control with no attribution.

how_to_obtain.instruction: List SIEM users and look for generic/shared privileged accounts instead of named per-person accounts.
how_to_obtain.command: splunk list user; splunk btool authorize list --debug
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Named per-person accounts mapped to scoped roles (secure) vs a shared admin account used by multiple operators (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: Splunk About securing the Splunk platform (RBAC / secure the default admin account)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview operators to confirm no shared/team credential is used for privileged SIEM access.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Confirmation that every privileged login maps to one named individual; no shared admin credential in circulation

option_description: Whether the default SIEM admin account has been removed or its default password (e.g. admin/changeme) replaced.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Stolen credentials / weak RBAC on the SIEM" — fires when default_accounts_removed_or_changed is false, giving any adversary trivial valid-account access via a known default credential (T1078).

how_to_obtain.instruction: List users and confirm the default 'admin' account is removed or no longer holds a default password.
how_to_obtain.command: splunk list user; splunk btool authorize list --debug
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No default 'admin' with default password; named accounts in use (secure) vs default admin/changeme still present (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: Splunk About securing the Splunk platform (RBAC / secure the default admin account)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt (with authorization) a login with the vendor default credential to prove it no longer works.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Default credential login is rejected (secure) vs default credential still grants access (insecure)

option_description: Whether the SIEM records its own administrative/access activity (config changes, role changes, feed enable/disable, audit-log access) and restricts access to that self-audit trail to a privileged subset (AU-9 / PCI DSS 10.2.x).
security_impact: An OR-trigger for the exposure "Stolen credentials / weak RBAC on the SIEM" — fires when audit_management_restricted_to_privileged_subset is false, so an insider can disable feeds or delete rules without the action being recorded (silent blinding).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the SIEM self-audit index is populated with recent admin/search/auth activity.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Recent admin/search/auth events present in the _audit index (secure) vs empty or auditing disabled (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: Splunk About securing the Splunk platform (use auditing to track activity)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm start/stop/pause of the audit pipeline and access to audit logs are themselves logged and that audit-log access is restricted.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Evidence that start/stop/pause of the audit pipeline and access to audit logs are themselves logged (PCI DSS 10.2.6/10.2.7) and that audit-log access is restricted (AU-9)
how_to_obtain.source: PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 10; NIST SP 800-53 AU-9 Protection of Audit Information

option_description: Whether the SIEM web UI and management/search API (Splunk Web 8000, splunkd management 8089, Wazuh dashboard) are bound to an internal/management network or sit behind VPN/ZTNA and are NOT reachable from untrusted/public networks.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers (AND-paired with the patch/CVE triggers) for the exposure "Internet-exposed SIEM UI/API and unpatched RCE" — fires when edge_management_interfaces_not_internet_reachable is false, turning the detection backbone into a directly attackable surface (T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Scan the SIEM's public IP for management/UI ports from an untrusted network vantage point.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Management/UI ports filtered from untrusted networks (secure) vs 8000/8089/dashboard open to the internet (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Top 10 A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration; MITRE ATT&CK T1190

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the UI/management network binding (interface ACLs, VPN/ZTNA front) limits reachability to the management network.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Evidence the UI/management API is bound to an internal/management network or fronted by VPN/ZTNA; only ingest ports reachable from monitored zones

option_description: Whether the SIEM control-plane / management+search API is not reachable from the public internet (restricted to the management network or fronted by VPN/ZTNA). Mirrors the UI exposure at API granularity.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers (AND-paired with the patch/CVE triggers) for the exposure "Internet-exposed SIEM UI/API and unpatched RCE" — fires when control_plane_api_not_publicly_exposed is false, exposing the control-plane API to direct exploitation of known SIEM CVEs.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe the splunkd management API port (8089) and Wazuh API from a public vantage point.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Control-plane/API ports filtered from the public internet (secure) vs 8089/API listening on a public interface (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Top 10 A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration; MITRE ATT&CK T1190

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the management API bind address restricts it to the management network.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Management API bound to an internal/management address (secure) vs bound to 0.0.0.0 / a public interface (insecure)

option_description: Whether the SIEM is running a software version below the fixed maintenance release for a known RCE CVE (e.g. Splunk unsafe-deserialization RCE CVE-2024-53247, CVE-2024-45733, CVE-2024-36985). True is the insecure/firing value.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers (AND-paired with the exposure triggers) for the exposure "Internet-exposed SIEM UI/API and unpatched RCE" — fires when unpatched_known_rce_cve is true; an exposed instance with an unpatched known RCE is a single-step full compromise of the detection capability.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the running Splunk version and compare it against the vendor advisory fixed releases.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Version at/above the fixed release for all applicable advisories (e.g. >= 9.2.3/9.1.6 for CVE-2024-45733; >= 9.3.2/9.2.4/9.1.7 for CVE-2024-53247) (secure) vs older (insecure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Cross-check the version against the current Splunk advisory list (SVD-2024 series) for any unpatched RCE id.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No applicable RCE advisory left unpatched for the running version (secure) vs at least one fixed-release RCE not yet applied (insecure)

option_description: Whether the SIEM software is kept at the current supported version with the latest security maintenance release applied inside the defined patch SLA — the broader patch-hygiene companion to unpatched_known_rce_cve.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Internet-exposed SIEM UI/API and unpatched RCE" — fires when edge_appliance_patched_within_sla is false (behind the fixed release and outside the patch window), even where a specific RCE id is not yet attributed.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the running version and compare against the current supported maintenance release.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Version at the current supported release with the latest security maintenance release (secure) vs behind the latest release and outside SLA (insecure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the patch SLA and the date the latest maintenance release was applied versus its publication date.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Evidence the latest maintenance release was applied within the defined patch window (secure) vs an overdue patch gap (insecure)

option_description: Whether bounded ingest queues and overflow handling protect the SIEM against log-flood DoS — when a source spikes, queues are capped and excess is shed/throttled rather than silently exhausting index storage/license and dropping real events.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Log flood / index-flooding denial of service" — fires when log_flood_overflow_protection is false (unbounded ingest), so a high-volume injection fills the index and blinds detection by overload.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect per-source ingest throughput and queue behaviour in the internal metrics log.
how_to_obtain.command: splunk search 'index=_internal source=*metrics.log group=per_source_thruput | timechart sum(kb) by series'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Per-source throughput baselined with bounded queues / controlled shedding under spike (secure) vs unbounded ingest with no shedding (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1498 Network Denial of Service; CIS Controls v8 Control 8 (8.3 adequate log storage)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm queue/overflow limits exist and excess is shed/throttled in a controlled way rather than ageing out real events.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented bounded-queue / overflow-shedding behaviour proven not to drop in-window real events under flood

option_description: Whether per-source ingest volume is baselined and a sudden spike against that baseline raises an alert, so a log flood from a compromised or spoofing source is detected rather than burying real alerts in noise.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Log flood / index-flooding denial of service" — fires when per_source_volume_baselining is false (no per-source spike alerting), so a flood goes undetected.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect per-source throughput series and confirm a baseline + spike alert exists.
how_to_obtain.command: splunk search 'index=_internal source=*metrics.log group=per_source_thruput | timechart sum(kb) by series'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Per-source throughput baselined with alerting on sudden spikes (secure) vs no volume monitoring (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1498 Network Denial of Service; CIS Controls v8 Control 8 (8.3 adequate log storage)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a scheduled anomaly/spike alert fires on per-source volume deviation, not merely a dashboard.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An active per-source volume-spike alert with evidence of delivery (secure) vs none (insecure)

option_description: Whether index storage is sized with headroom so events survive the required retention window and a flood cannot exhaust capacity and force early rotation/overwrite of real events.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Log flood / index-flooding denial of service" — fires when log_storage_sized_for_retention is false (no headroom monitoring), so a volume surge ages out events before review and destroys the detection record.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read indexes.conf retention and size caps to confirm storage is sized so events are not aged out before the retention window.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: frozenTimePeriodInSecs >= 7776000 (90 days) and storage sized so events are not aged out by maxTotalDataSizeMB before that (secure) vs size-driven early rotation (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: Splunk indexes.conf retention settings; CIS Controls v8 Control 8 (8.3/8.10)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check current index disk usage/headroom against the configured size caps.
how_to_obtain.command: splunk search '| dbinspect index=* | stats sum(sizeOnDiskMB) by index'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Disk usage well below maxTotalDataSizeMB with monitored headroom (secure) vs at/near the cap with no headroom monitoring (insecure)

option_description: Whether network-layer DoS protection (rate limiting / scrubbing / per-source connection and bandwidth controls) shields the SIEM ingest endpoints from high-volume flood traffic.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Log flood / index-flooding denial of service" — fires when ddos_protection_in_place is false (ingest ports accept unbounded inbound volume), allowing a flood to overwhelm ingestion.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm network-layer DoS controls (rate limiting, scrubbing, per-source connection/bandwidth caps) front the ingest endpoints.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Evidence of rate limiting / scrubbing / per-source connection and bandwidth controls on the ingest endpoints (secure) vs unbounded inbound volume with no DoS controls (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1498 Network Denial of Service; CIS Controls v8 Control 8 (8.3 adequate log storage)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the firewall/load-balancer/proxy config in front of the ingest ports for per-source rate/connection limits.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Per-source connection/bandwidth rate limits configured on the ingest path (secure) vs no limits (insecure)

option_description: Whether secrets, credentials, and tokens are masked/redacted before or at index time (e.g. Splunk SEDCMD / props.conf anonymization or an ingest-time filter) so the SIEM does not become a high-value plaintext credential store (CWE-532; OWASP ASVS V7).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Unmasked secrets/PII in the index; coverage and retention gaps" — fires when secrets_masked_in_logs is false (raw passwords/keys/tokens indexed verbatim).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep props.conf for SEDCMD masking rules covering secret/token patterns.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SEDCMD rules masking known secret/PII patterns at index time (secure) vs none and a search showing plaintext secrets in raw events (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE CWE-532 Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File; OWASP ASVS V7 Error Handling and Logging

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run a targeted search for common secret patterns to prove they are not indexed in cleartext.
how_to_obtain.command: splunk search 'index=* (password=* OR "api_key" OR "Authorization: Bearer") | head 20'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No raw secrets returned / values masked (secure) vs plaintext passwords/keys/tokens in raw events (insecure)

option_description: Whether regulated PII (PAN, government IDs, sensitive personal data) is excluded or masked from indexed events, so the index is not a high-value plaintext PII store and GDPR/PCI exposure.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Unmasked secrets/PII in the index; coverage and retention gaps" — fires when pii_excluded_from_logs is false (regulated PII indexed verbatim).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep props.conf for SEDCMD/anonymization rules masking PAN, government IDs, and sensitive personal fields.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SEDCMD rules masking known PII patterns at index time (secure) vs none and a search showing plaintext PII in raw events (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE CWE-532 Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File; OWASP ASVS V7 Error Handling and Logging

how_to_obtain.instruction: Search for PAN/government-ID patterns to prove regulated PII is not indexed verbatim.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No matches / values masked (secure) vs PAN-like or government-ID PII present in raw events (insecure)

option_description: Online retention window in days for indexed events (Splunk frozenTimePeriodInSecs / index sizing). The forensic minimum is 90 days (CIS Control 8.3/8.10).
security_impact: An OR-trigger for the exposure "Unmasked secrets/PII in the index; coverage and retention gaps" — fires when retention is below 90 days, since too-short retention destroys evidence and creates a forensic blind spot.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read frozenTimePeriodInSecs (and the size cap) from indexes.conf and convert to days (>= 7776000s = 90 days).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: frozenTimePeriodInSecs >= 7776000 (90 days) and storage sized so events are not aged out by maxTotalDataSizeMB before that (secure) vs short frozenTimePeriodInSecs or size-driven early rotation (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: Splunk indexes.conf retention settings; CIS Controls v8 Control 8 (8.3/8.10)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the oldest event actually present per index meets the configured retention window.
how_to_obtain.command: splunk search '| tstats min(_time) as oldest where index=* by index | eval days_retained=round((now()-oldest)/86400,1)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Oldest events span >= 90 days (secure) vs the index holding less than the configured/required window (insecure)

option_description: Whether the SIEM and all log sources synchronize time against a trusted source (NTP, consistent UTC) so correlated events share a coherent timeline (CIS Control 8.4).
security_impact: An OR-trigger for the exposure "Unmasked secrets/PII in the index; coverage and retention gaps" — fires when clocks_synced_to_trusted_time_source is false (clock skew breaks correlation and enables timestomping, T1070.006).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check NTP synchronization status on the SIEM host (and sample sources).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: System clock synchronized: yes, with a reachable NTP source (secure) vs unsynchronized / large offset (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 Audit Log Management (8.4 standardize time synchronization)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm all log sources standardize on NTP and consistent UTC timestamps in indexed events.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented NTP/UTC standardization across all sources and the SIEM (secure) vs inconsistent timezones in indexed events (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 Audit Log Management (8.4 standardize time synchronization)

option_description: Whether the index store volumes / object store are encrypted at rest (AES-256 or cloud-managed KMS keys) so disk/snapshot theft does not disclose the indexed credentials, PII, and sensitive payloads (NIST SP 800-92; OWASP Cryptographic Storage).
security_impact: An OR-trigger for the exposure "Unmasked secrets/PII in the index; coverage and retention gaps" — fires when encrypted_at_rest is false (indexes on unencrypted volumes).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the index storage volumes / object store use at-rest encryption with managed keys (KMS/HSM) separate from the data.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Evidence that the index storage volumes / object store use at-rest encryption with managed keys (KMS/HSM) separate from data; NIST 800-92 notes logs may capture sensitive information and require confidentiality protection
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-92 Guide to Computer Security Log Management; OWASP Cryptographic Storage Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: On a Linux SIEM host, check whether the index volume is on an encrypted block device.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Index mount sits on a LUKS/crypt device or cloud-encrypted volume (secure) vs plain unencrypted volume (insecure)
